Subject: Order form questions: invoices split & VAT responsibility

Quick follow on the order form we received this morning. Finance has three items they need clarity on before they can route payment: 

1) Can we split the first year invoicing into three tranches tied to milestones (kickoff, volume ramp, go-live)?
2) How will minimum commit credits be applied if we tranche invoices and the usage is uneven across tranches?
3) Which party is responsible for VAT/withholding — our team is in Madrid so we need this explicitly spelled out.

Attached is our internal PO template (finance@pillar-analytics.com). Can you confirm if Redwood can accept staged invoices and whether you can provide VAT evidence for the billed entity?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Subject: internal: OF tranching + min-commit logic

Mina / Team — quick internal notes on Claudia’s ask.

Points I want captured in the OF redline:
- Invoice tranches: three invoices, each net30 from issue date. Milestones are contractual (kickoff, 50% ramp, production go-live).
- Min-commit application: credits are accrued by tranche at the pro rata rate of the annual commit. If usage for a tranche exceeds the pro rata allocation, it consumes overage; if below, unused credit carries forward to next tranche within the contract year. We need a one-line reconciliation table and a sample calculation.
- Net terms: Redwood prefers net30 but sales can accept net45 for first year with a finance fee unless deal exec approves otherwise.
- VAT/Withholding: If Pillar requires Redwood EU invoicing, Legal needs Pillar’s VAT ID + registered entity. If Redwood invoices from US, Pillar must handle any local VAT withholding; we will provide tax evidence (W-9 / US EIN) and a VAT exemption letter where applicable.

Kimberly / Ben — any objections to carrying the reconciliation table in an appendix to the OF and including our W-9 in attachments?

Karthik
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:07:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: internal: OF tranching + min-commit logic

Adding legal perspective — a few redline asks: 

1) Make the tranches milestone-based with objective acceptance criteria (e.g., "ramp = sustained 30-day volume >= X tokens") so disputes are minimized.
2) For carry-forward credits, cap carry-forward to 25% of annual commit to avoid open-ended exposure.
3) Net terms: we can accept net45 but require a one-time finance provisioning fee (0.5% of committed value) unless Sales/Finance approve waiver.
4) VAT: we will provide W-9 and Redwood US EIN. If Pillar insists on Redwood EU invoicing, require their VAT ID + confirmation of non-withholding in writing.

I’ll redline the OF and produce a short appendix with the reconciliation calculation and an example. Attaching redline draft (redline_order_form_20261113.pdf).

— Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

- We accepted the 3-tranche split tied to the milestones you proposed. Each tranche will be invoiced net30.
- Min-commit credits will be applied pro rata per tranche; unused credit rolls forward but capped at 25% of annual commit (see appendix table, page 2 of redline).
- We can invoice from Redwood US (EIN included) and provide W-9; if Pillar requires Redwood EU invoicing, please share your EU VAT ID and confirmation of non-withholding so Legal can approve.
- Net terms: default net30. We can set net45 for Year 1 subject to a 0.5% provisioning fee (included as a separate line item) unless Pillar requests waiver and we get finance approval.

Ask from Pillar: please confirm the billing entity and whether the PO needs taxes shown line-item or if a gross invoice is acceptable. Once we have that, Legal will finalize the OF redline and I’ll push the DocuSign.

If helpful, I can schedule a 20-min call Monday to walk through the appendix and the sample reconciliation.

Thanks — Mina
